# Disagreement Log — Gospel of Thomas, Saying 19

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Saying:** GTH 019
**Total Disagreements:** 3

---

## Disagreement 1 — "came into being before coming into being" vs. "existed before existing"

**Verse:** v.1
**EMET/LOGOS:** "came into being before coming into being"
**PNEUMA:** "existed before existing"
**Issue:** The Coptic *šōp* (to come into being / become) carries the specific sense of becoming, not merely existing. The paradox is about the threshold of existence, not simply the state.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Came into being before coming into being" — the Coptic vocabulary of becoming preserved.

---

## Disagreement 2 — "do not change" vs. "never change"

**Verse:** v.3
**EMET/LOGOS:** "do not change"
**PNEUMA:** "never change"
**Issue:** Intensifier "never" not in the Coptic. The simple negation is more precise.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Do not change" retained.

---

## Disagreement 3 — "will not taste death" vs. "will never die"

**Verse:** v.4
**EMET/LOGOS:** "will not taste death"
**PNEUMA:** "will never die"
**Issue:** Recurring idiom; consistent rendering across Sayings 1, 18, 19 reveals the structural pattern.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Will not taste death" maintained throughout.

---
